topic: Would you trust a robot home alone? What home humanoids have actually shown
label: Illustrative animation

master_direction.logline: The BrewIQ host walks in on a robot doing his chores, follows it room to room, sees it miss and recover, then discovers there can be a human behind the controls.
master_direction.style: Premium 3D animated short film in the BrewIQ brand look (midnight navy, electric cyan, vibrant blue, warm amber, clean white). Feature-animation characters in one consistent, detailed apartment; cinematic lighting and depth of field; real camera grammar; no presenter-on-a-slide, no flat backgrounds, no floating text cards.
master_direction.arc: Wonder (0–10s) → doubt: the miss (10–13.5s) → respect: the retry (13.5–16.5s) → twist: the human in the loop (16.5–20s) → question to the viewer (20–24s).
master_direction.story_rule: A new meaningful visual event every 2–4s (see each scene's events); no shot holds without a change.
master_direction.host_rule: The host is a participant, not a pointer: he walks in, watches, crouches, winces, nods, and speaks to camera once at the end. No pointing poses.
master_direction.accuracy: Illustrative animation of a generic robot, not Figure's or 1X's design. Chores shown are the ones Figure tested (towels, toys; beds are named in the voiceover). The miss and retry dramatise Figure's 56% full-task rate and its reported self-correction. The remote operator dramatises 1X's scheduled Expert for chores NEO doesn't know, labelled 'Different robot: 1X NEO'.

character.name: BrewIQ host
character.lock_prompt: CHARACTER LOCK — the BrewIQ host: the man in the reference image, about 30, warm light-brown South Asian skin, short dark wavy hair, dark brown eyes, strong dark eyebrows, light stubble, friendly confident half-smile; plain black quilted jacket with no logo or brand mark; no glasses. Identical face, hair, outfit and proportions to the reference image; never change clothing or colors; natural weight and follow-through in every movement.
rules: Matches the sheet: black wavy hair, no glasses, black hooded quilted jacket (his 'black hoodie'), black tee, black joggers, white sneakers.
Not in the first 1.8s; the robot's action is the hook. He enters through the door at 2.4s.
Every scene gives him a different action: enter, set keys down, crouch and lean in, wince, nod, lean on the island and turn to camera. No repeated gestures and no pointing.
Speaks to camera once (Scene 7). Mouth movement only in the clip; the line comes from the voiceover track.
Absent from Scene 6 (remote workroom). The lock stays in that prompt for pipeline consistency, with an explicit 'does not appear' line.
If a clip drifts (face, hair, jacket), regenerate it; do not fix it in the grade.

rules: Same apartment, furniture layout and amber-sunrise-on-navy light in Scenes 1–5 and 7.

typography.hook_zone: top_safe: headline box x 90, y 300, 690×280px on 1080×1920 (see composition.zones)
rules: One headline at a time, never stacked; 2–6 words, max 2 lines, 84/76/68px bold rounded sans, clean white on a 85% midnight-navy plate with a cyan accent.

Headlines sit in the top safe band and never enter the presenter zone (y 620–1360); every prompt keeps faces and heads below the top 30%, so text never sits behind a character. Composite text as the top layer.

Small persistent 'Illustrative animation' tag top-left (x 90, y 250) for the full runtime; BrewIQ end card in the last 0.8s.

voiceover_instructions.voice: Warm, conversational natural American English; curious on the hook, lightly amused, never alarmist.
voiceover_instructions.tone: Curious on the hook; confident and clear on explanations; expressive but not theatrical.
voiceover_instructions.pauses: Natural 0.3–0.5s pause before each reveal (the catch and the payoff).
voiceover_instructions.track: Record narration as its own audio track; mute all model-generated audio.
voiceover_instructions.loudness: Voice integrated -14 LUFS; true peak below -1 dBTP.
voiceover_instructions.pace: 145–160 WPM (about 2.5 words per second). 'THIS robot' stressed; a 0.4s pause before 'When it missed' and before 'Another robot'; 'So who's really home?' slower, direct, matched to the host's mouth in Scene 7.

subtitles.text: it stepped back and tried again.

subtitle_instructions: Phrase captions, max 6 words, lower safe band. White with soft shadow; '56%' wording stays as spoken ('fifty-six percent').

sfx.sfx: Soft servo whir as the robot turns its head
Two wooden toys clack into the basket

Whoosh through the lens; kitchen room tone
Tiny servo whir on the robot's head turn

sound.music: Light plucked-string and soft-piano motif (~96 BPM) from 0s; drops to a single held note at 12.2s for the miss, resolves warmly at 14.4s; cooler, sparser pad 16.5–20s; returns warm and ends on an unresolved chord under the final line.
sound.veo_audio: Mute all Veo-generated audio; build sound in the edit.

assembly: Generate each scene as its own 4s Veo clip at 9:16 with the three character references; trim to the scene window (3.0–4.0s each).
